title: SQL Foundations
subtitle: Learn to read tables, write SELECT queries, filter rows, sort results, and handle real-world beginner data.
intendedFor: web developers who need SQL basics
learningGoals: Explain what SQL does in plain language.
Identify tables, rows, columns, records, fields, and simple keys.
Write basic SELECT queries against one table.
Choose specific columns instead of always using SELECT *.
Filter rows with WHERE.
Compare text and numeric values.
Combine conditions with AND, OR, and NOT.
Sort results with ORDER BY.
Limit output with LIMIT.
Search text using LIKE and wildcards.
Filter lists and ranges using IN, NOT IN, and BETWEEN.
Find missing values using IS NULL and IS NOT NULL.
Read query results and explain them in plain English.

modules.title: Getting Started with SQL
modules.purpose: Build the learner's mental model before syntax: what SQL is, how databases organize information, and how questions become queries.
learningObjectives: Explain what SQL is used for in real applications.
Identify tables, rows, columns, records, and fields.
Read simple table data and describe what it means.
Use the browser SQL workspace to run a beginner query.

topics.title: SQL, Databases, and Tables
topics.summary: Learn the one foundation you need before querying: SQL asks databases for results, and database tables organize values into rows and columns.
learningGoals: Explain that SQL is used to ask structured data for useful results.
Describe a database table using rows (records) and columns (fields).
Use table and column names to identify which data a question needs.

topics.title: First SQL Environment
topics.summary: Use the editor, Tables view, Run action, and Results view, then execute one tiny SQL statement.
learningGoals: Locate the SQL editor, Tables view, Run action, and Results view.
Run one small SQL statement and inspect the returned result.
Check available data before writing a query.

topics.title: Module 0 Student Roster Project
topics.summary: Build a simple student roster snapshot one safe SELECT step at a time until the final table is ready to share.
learningGoals: Keep a small SQL project growing from one working query to the next.
Read a student table by selecting the columns needed for a clear roster view.

modules.moduleProject: Create a simple data map for a tiny school or store database showing tables, columns, and example rows.
modules.summary: Understand tables, use the SQL workspace, and finish with a short roster project.

modules.title: Reading Data with SELECT
modules.purpose: Teach learners to retrieve data confidently with SELECT and FROM before filtering or joining tables.
learningObjectives: Write SELECT queries that retrieve data from one table.
Choose specific columns instead of always selecting every column.
Use FROM to identify the table being queried.
Read a query result table and explain what was returned.

topics.title: Selecting Data with SELECT and FROM
topics.summary: Learn SELECT and FROM once: choose the columns to return, choose the source table, and build readable multi-column results.
learningGoals: Use SELECT to choose result columns and FROM to name the source table.
Choose between SELECT * and explicit columns based on what the task needs.
Select several columns with commas and control their left-to-right result order.

topics.title: Reading and Fixing SELECT Queries
topics.summary: Predict the shape of a simple result and repair common SELECT, comma, FROM, and table-name mistakes.
learningGoals: Predict which columns a simple SELECT query will return before running it.
Recognize missing commas, missing FROM, and incorrect table names.
Repair a broken single-table SELECT query using a short syntax checklist.

topics.title: Module 1 Product Starter Sheet Project
topics.summary: Build a clean product starter sheet by growing one SELECT query into a simple reference report.
learningGoals: Carry a product query forward from one finished step to the next.
Select only the product columns that make a report easier to read.

modules.moduleProject: Build a starter query sheet with beginner SELECT queries against a products table.
modules.summary: Choose columns, read them from one table, fix simple syntax mistakes, and build a short product handoff.

modules.title: Filtering Rows
modules.purpose: Introduce decision-making in queries by teaching learners to keep only the rows they actually need.
learningObjectives: Use WHERE to return only rows that match a condition.
Compare text and numbers with beginner SQL operators.
Combine conditions with AND, OR, and NOT.
Debug common filtering mistakes in simple SQL queries.

topics.title: Filtering with WHERE and Comparisons
topics.summary: Use WHERE with exact, not-equal, strict, and inclusive comparisons, and format number and text literals correctly.
learningGoals: Place WHERE after FROM and translate one plain-language filter into a condition.
Choose among =, <>, >, <, >=, and <= based on the requirement and boundary.
Write numeric literals without quotes and text literals with single quotes.

topics.title: Combining Conditions
topics.summary: Combine filters with AND and OR, group mixed logic with parentheses, use NOT deliberately, and debug conditions against the requirement.
learningGoals: Use AND for simultaneous requirements and OR for acceptable alternatives.
Use parentheses to make mixed AND/OR logic explicit.
Use NOT only when its scope is clear and debug one filtering condition at a time.

topics.title: Module 2 Inventory Watchlist Project
topics.summary: Build an inventory watchlist by adding one practical filter at a time to the same working query.
learningGoals: Refine one inventory query through multiple filtering steps.
Use comparisons and logical conditions to isolate the products that need attention.

modules.moduleProject: Create a data-detective worksheet with filtering prompts and SQL answers.
modules.summary: Filter rows with comparisons and logical conditions, then build a practical inventory watchlist.

modules.title: Sorting and Limiting Results
modules.purpose: Help beginners control output so answers are easier to read, rank, and compare.
learningObjectives: Sort query results with ORDER BY.
Use ASC and DESC to control sort direction.
Use LIMIT to show a smaller result set.
Combine filtering, sorting, and limiting in one query.

topics.title: Sorting with ORDER BY
topics.summary: Sort results with ORDER BY, choose ASC or DESC, and add a secondary column when ties need a predictable order.
learningGoals: Use ORDER BY after row selection to control result sequence without changing row membership.
Choose ASC or DESC from requirement language such as earliest, latest, smallest, or largest.
Use a second ORDER BY column as a tie-breaker when the primary sort can repeat.

topics.title: Ranked Results with LIMIT
topics.summary: Sort first, then use LIMIT to return a meaningful top-N or bottom-N result.
learningGoals: Explain why LIMIT alone does not define a ranking.
Place LIMIT after ORDER BY in a ranked query.
Combine filtering, ordering, and LIMIT for top-N or bottom-N requests.

topics.title: Module 3 Sales Leaderboard Project
topics.summary: Turn a rough product query into a ranked leaderboard by layering sorting and limiting steps one by one.
learningGoals: Grow a ranking query from a plain result set into a focused leaderboard.
Use ORDER BY and LIMIT to make a product report easy to scan.

modules.moduleProject: Build a ranked product report using sorting and limiting.
modules.summary: Order rows predictably, build ranked top-N results, and finish with a cumulative sales leaderboard.

modules.title: Advanced Filtering
modules.purpose: Expand filtering to real-world cases like partial text, multiple choices, ranges, and missing values.
learningObjectives: Search partial text with LIKE and wildcards.
Filter multiple values with IN and NOT IN.
Filter ranges with BETWEEN.
Find missing and present values with IS NULL and IS NOT NULL.

topics.title: LIKE and Wildcards
topics.summary: Use LIKE with % for variable-length text and _ for exactly one character.
learningGoals: Use LIKE when a text pattern is needed instead of an exact equality check.
Use % for prefixes, suffixes, and contained fragments.
Use _ when exactly one character may vary at a specific position.

topics.title: IN and BETWEEN
topics.summary: Use IN for exact value sets and BETWEEN for inclusive lower-and-upper ranges.
learningGoals: Use IN and NOT IN for allowed or excluded exact values.
Use BETWEEN for an inclusive range with correctly ordered boundaries.
Choose a list or range operator that matches the requirement instead of repeating comparisons.

topics.title: NULL and Combined Filters
topics.summary: Use IS NULL and IS NOT NULL for missing values, then combine presence and text rules clearly.
learningGoals: Distinguish NULL from empty text or zero and avoid = NULL.
Use IS NULL and IS NOT NULL for missing-value checks.
Combine NULL checks with LIKE, AND, OR, and parentheses for cleanup rules.

topics.title: Module 4 Customer Cleanup Project
topics.summary: Build a cumulative customer-cleanup report with NULL, exact-value, text-pattern, and test-record filters.
learningGoals: Carry a correct SQL query forward across cumulative project milestones.
Combine NULL checks, exact-value filters, LIKE patterns, and AND conditions.
Produce a final cleanup result that satisfies a concrete stakeholder handoff.

modules.moduleProject: Create a search-and-cleanup worksheet for a customer table with missing or inconsistent information.
modules.summary: Match text patterns, filter sets and ranges, handle missing values, and finish with a cumulative customer-cleanup report.

modules.title: Capstone: Customer Follow-Up Report
modules.purpose: Pull the course skills together in one final reporting task that feels like a beginner analyst handoff.
learningObjectives: Combine selection, filtering, ordering, and limiting in one practical query flow.
Revise a working query without losing earlier progress.
Build a clean report that highlights real customer follow-up needs.

topics.title: Module 5 Customer Follow-Up Capstone
topics.summary: Build a cumulative stakeholder report using status lists, NULL checks, exact-value filters, ranges, LIKE, ORDER BY, and LIMIT.
learningGoals: Carry a correct SQL query forward through four cumulative stakeholder requirements.
Combine IN, IS NOT NULL, exact comparisons, BETWEEN, and LIKE in one readable WHERE clause.
Apply ORDER BY before LIMIT so the final five-row handoff is deterministic.
Preserve approved requirements while extending a query instead of rewriting it from scratch.

projectBrief.scenario: A community outreach coordinator needs a concise customer follow-up list built from the cleanup table. The report must keep only useful, contactable records and rank the most recent signups first.
projectBrief.role: Junior SQL analyst preparing a customer follow-up handoff
projectBrief.workspace: Browser SQL editor, customers table schema, and deterministic results table
projectBrief.deliverable: One four-step cumulative customer follow-up query that combines the core SQL Foundations skills without losing earlier requirements.
requirements: Keep one valid SELECT statement in every step.
Use the previous complete solution as the next starter query.
Preserve every earlier requirement unless the current step explicitly replaces it.
Use only SQL concepts taught in SQL Foundations.
Finish with deterministic ordering and a practical row limit.

stepLadder.title: Build the Follow-Up Candidate List
stepLadder.requirement: Return the requested customer columns and keep only records whose status is active or draft using IN.

stepLadder.title: Keep Contactable Customers
stepLadder.requirement: Preserve the candidate list and require a non-missing email address with IS NOT NULL.

stepLadder.title: Apply the Date and Text Rules
stepLadder.requirement: Keep all prior filters, add the authored signup-date range with BETWEEN, and exclude test-style names with a LIKE-based condition.

stepLadder.title: Rank and Limit the Final Handoff
stepLadder.requirement: Preserve every filter, sort the newest signups first with a stable secondary sort, and limit the report to the requested number of rows.

modules.moduleProject: Create a final customer follow-up report that surfaces the most important real records for a teammate to review.
